title: Trans-Workflow | Turn one-off AI chats into reusable workflows
description: Trans-Workflow chains prompts, AI skills and several models into one workflow: build it once, run it again and again. Nothing to install, data stays in your browser, and results export to a single web page.
ogTitle: Trans-Workflow | Turn one-off AI chats into reusable workflows
ogDescription: Chain prompts, AI skills and models into one workflow: build once, run repeatedly.
wf.logo.title: TransWeb home
wf.hero.desc: No backend to write, no server to deploy. Pick a ready-made workflow, or chain a few skills into your own. If one node drifts, rerun just that node, fix a line, and carry on.
wf.hero.meta: No server cost · data stays in your browser · MIT licensed

wf.market.desc: Curated workflows for teaching, content, data, research and legal review — open one and run it

wf.features.title: Why a single file?
wf.f1.title: Double-click to run — nothing to deploy
wf.f1.text: One HTML file is the whole engine: no Docker, no database. Download it, double-click, done.
wf.f2.title: Fix one node, not the whole run
wf.f2.text: A node went off track? Don't start over: rerun that node on its own, or stop and correct it by hand, then keep going.
wf.f3.title: Your data stays on your machine
wf.f3.text: Run logs, intermediate results and final deliverables all live in your browser and are never uploaded. Sensitive contracts, papers and business plans are safe.
wf.steps.title: Three steps to a running workflow.
wf.step1.title: Pick an AI workflow
wf.step1.text: Choose one from the marketplace; it opens ready to use.
wf.step2.title: Describe your need, then run
wf.step2.text: Your request goes to the first node and the rest run in order. Want to change something? Stop at any time.
wf.step3.title: Export the result page
wf.step3.text: The whole workflow's output becomes a shareable, deliverable web page in one click.
wf.builder.title: Chain skills into one workflow.
wf.builder.desc: Like building blocks: pick a skill, order the nodes, connect the data.
wf.b1.title: Pick a skill
wf.b1.text: Choose one from SkillHub, or create your own.
wf.b2.title: Order the nodes
wf.b2.text: Lay the nodes out in the order they should run.
wf.b3.title: Wire the data
wf.b3.text: Feed one node's output into the next node's input.
wf.b4.title: Export a web page
wf.b4.text: Pack the workflow into one HTML file: double-click to run, share it as is.
wf.arch.title: One workflow, two views.
wf.arch.desc: Same thing, two questions: what runs first, and where does the data go?
wf.svg.legendSolid: Solid: data flow (A→B, A→C, B→D, C→D)
wf.personas.title: Who uses Trans-Workflow
wf.personas.desc: You are not chatting with a bot — you are running a workflow that hands you a finished deliverable.
wf.pain.label: Pain points
wf.p1.quote: “If you are a teacher, turn quadratic functions into animated graphs, a tiered problem set and a mock exam.”
wf.p1.pain: Visual courseware is hard · writing problems takes hours · tiered teaching rarely happens
wf.p2.quote: “If you are revising, turn one wrong answer into a set of variants that test the same idea in a new skin.”
wf.p2.pain: The same mistakes repeat · the method does not transfer · abstract ideas stay abstract
wf.p3.quote: “If you are in-house counsel, drop in a contract and get a review report with risk levels and suggested edits.”
wf.p3.pain: Line-by-line review is slow · risks get missed · write-ups eat time
wf.cases.title: One input, one finished deliverable.
wf.cases.desc: No need to imagine it — see what goes in, how it flows, and what comes out.
wf.uc.t.input: Around the properties of a quadrangular prism, write a problem that covers both a geometric proof and a computation.
wf.uc.t.note: Every node can pause for a human check — fix one line and keep going instead of rerunning everything.
wf.uc.s.step2: Paste a problem you keep getting wrong
wf.uc.s.input: As shown, the parabola y = -x² + 2x + 3 meets the x-axis at A and B (A left of B) and the y-axis at C, with vertex D. Find the coordinates of A, B, C, D and the area of quadrilateral ACBD.
wf.uc.s.step3: It diagnoses the error first, then builds variants
wf.uc.s.note: Change the numbers, the conditions, the wording — drill the same idea until it sticks.
wf.uc.l.step2: Paste the clause (or the whole contract)
wf.uc.l.input: Clause 5.2: if Party B delivers late, it shall pay liquidated damages per day, with the amount to be agreed separately…
wf.uc.l.note: Five nodes share the job: split the contract into structured clauses, run the basic checks, assess commercial and compliance risk in parallel, then merge everything into one report.
wf.community.title: Open source, and more than the code
wf.community.desc: Workflows, skills, docs and the engine itself are all open to contributions
wf.faq.q1: How does it compare with traditional AI workflow platforms (Dify, Coze)?
wf.cmp.r1b: Needs servers, Docker and a vector database, billed monthly
wf.cmp.r1c: No server cost — one HTML file just runs
wf.cmp.r2b: One bad step often means rerunning the whole chain and burning tokens
wf.cmp.r2c: Rerun a single node, with human review whenever you want
wf.cmp.r3b: Set up accounts, permissions and environment variables
wf.cmp.r3c: Send the HTML file; a double-click is all it takes
wf.faq.q2: Why is single-file better than a cloud workflow?
wf.faq.a2: Single-file means zero ops, easy archiving and effortless sharing. One workflow is one HTML file: keep it alongside your documents, open it whenever you need it, and a server outage cannot take it down.
wf.faq.q3: How do I share a workflow with someone else?
wf.faq.a3: Export the HTML file and send it over — they double-click to run it. You can also put it back on a static server.
wf.faq.a4: The features are free. The engine is MIT-licensed open source: no sign-up or subscription, just open the page.
wf.faq.q5: Can I use my own API key?
wf.faq.a5: Yes. Use the built-in models or plug in your own API key; the key is stored only in your browser and never uploaded.
wf.faq.a6: Any mainstream model with an OpenAI-compatible API works, and you can switch per skill node.
wf.faq.q7: Can I embed Trans-Workflow in our existing system or product?
wf.faq.a7: Yes. Trans-Workflow is MIT-licensed and single-file: use it as the base for internal tooling or integrate it into an existing SaaS product — customise and commercialise freely.
